Announcing The Griddies for 2026!

Each year volunteers from The Academy here gather your votes to honor the best puzzle of the year in each category: M-W, TH, FRI-SAT, and SUN. Nominations for POYs will commence on December 1 and run until the 31st. After balloting in the first weeks of January, winners will be announced in the third week of January. Voting is easy, anonymous, and fun! Even more fun is going back through the archives of 2026 and noting your favorites. 

I can use some help! My fellow volunteers from last year are too committed to other projects this year, so right now it’s just me and Nora in France (thanks Nora!). If you’d like to help out with the Griddies, you’d be 1) drumming up participation in Comments, 2) writing up short descriptions of the nominated puzzles and 3) helping with coordinating the votes. If interested, please REPLY to this message and we’ll figure it out. It's not too much work and it's a great way to give back to this community which has given us so much joy.

I promise not to post this too often...
Aha, just belatedly got the theme. Fun even not knowing what was going on...

I'm not big on anagrams, and I usually don't pick up on them, so I solved this quickly as a slightly quirky themeless, and then pondered the revealer for a while before seeing the light. I think this is what some people would call a constructor's puzzle, but if I were an anagram lover I'd call it a solver's puzzle. This was indeed a scrabbly puzzle, Curran. Nice debut!

Fun concept. Also - 70 Across reminded me of this Mitch Hedberg classic - 

"I like an escalator, man, 'cause an escalator can never break. It can only become stairs. You should never see an 'Escalator Temporarily Out Of Order' sign, just 'Escalator Temporarily Stairs. Sorry for the convenience."

I solved the puzzle without getting the theme, and had to read Wordplay to find it out. I should just stick to polarimetry instead. 

By the way, looking forward to the giant puzzle supplement in tomorrow's print edition! I ordered extra copies for family members visiting for Thanksgiving, mostly so they keep their hands off mine.
Just came to say that I, too, completely missed the trick. Nice in retrospect but kinda more impressive that it was done at all rather than... puzzly?
A nice fresh crossword. The theme added nothing to my experience, I didn't pick up on the the anagram aspect until reading the word play column.

I figured out the revealer about halfway through, and a few minutes later, I got the 'aha' moment when trying to figure out how MORALITYREP was 'out of order.' Once I saw the trick, I was able to solve the other themed entries relatively easily.

Fun puzzle!

It takes moxie to debut on a Sunday, and it takes great skill to pull it off.  It also takes a creative constructor's mind to see the phrase TEMPORARILY OUT OF ORDER and envision this theme.  Very, very impressive debut.

And it’s an entertaining theme.  Because the theme answers aren’t typical crossword answers, they don’t just pop into the brain, and they are fun to guess at with as few crosses as possible.  

I loved the sweet cross of RIOJA and DJIBOUTI, and gave an inner thumbs up for [It rings a bell!] for HAMMER, a cluing angle that has never been used for that answer in any of the major outlets.

Oh, you’ve got me wanting to see more from you, Curran.  Congratulations on your Sunday debut, and thank you for a splendid outing!

Fun with anagrams! This fan CRUSH(ed) IT.

[Fake news]

REALITY ROMP

Congrats on the debut! 

If you haven't ever done so, it's fun to take your own (full) name and see what words you can make from it.
I had no idea what the themes had to do with anything so I solved it as themeless . But after reading the write up I m gobsmacked. Wow!!
Truly a light-bulb puzzle.  I saw it about half way through.  Very enjoyable.
That was fun!  Enjoyed the “aha” moment when it hit me. Congratulations on an impressive debut, Curran!  Looking forward to the next one.
This just so happens to be the second straight night I'm having AMARO with dessert

The Riemann hypothesis has been in the news.
Meh - I offer you CLM’s axiom:
“If, after finishing the puzzle and trying but failing to make sense of the theme, it will always be anagrams.”

Meanwhile, I thought it would be funny if “snatching, biting and screaming for tots” solved to VERBS.

On the fence with this as a solver today but pretty impressed as a constructor, so congrats on a remarkable debut from that standpoint for sure!

Overall I was in suspense the first half wondering what the revealer was going to be and it was very clever, and personally love some good anagrams. And once I got it, it helped with the second half solve. I can see where the constructor came from a scrabble background, I can just see him shifting the scrabble tiles around to construct these.

The rest of the grid and clues seemed pretty routine and made for a smooth if somewhat easy solve.

My main trauma today, as a Cincinnatian and animal lover, is seeing Fiona mentioned along with HIPPO today. Rest in peace.

This was one of the rare occasions on which I completed a Sunday NYT puzzle without ever comprehending the theme. When I finally looked it up, it made sense. Never occurred to me to add the invisible comma to the master clue, Temporarily, Out of Order.
I'm not able to print the "large print" version of the puzzle. Help please!
Brilliant

I was gobsmacked when I read what the theme was (I couldn't see it on my own).  

Great puzzle, lots of fun, especially when mis-parsing CRUSHIT.  

And HAKA shows up again.  I've never seen the word to my knowledge my whole life, and now I've seen it twice in a couple of months.

What a species we are--a side product of our appetite for illegal drugs ends up introducing the hippo to the New World.

And today I learned that what I thought was a U-trap is a P-trap.

Angrily attend the senior dance
IRATELY PROM

Review GTA VI before it officially came out
IMPORT EARLY

January 6th offender who made off with some mementos?
PALMY RIOTER

What we'll probably get once we oust Hegseth?
POLITER ARMY

What you need for your large Thanksgiving gathering?
PORTLIER YAM

What the Cowardly Lion might do, at most?
EMPTILY ROAR
Amazing puzzle! It was a great feeling when everything clicked for me

Wow! I went from not liking the theme in this puzzle at all to loving it once I read the explanation. Brilliant, brilliant puzzle. I didn’t get the theme at all when I was solving it, but it’s very smart.

A very original puzzle with a great variety of fill. And no junk.

I was halfway through and realized that the starred clue's answers were anagrams of each other, but only on reading Wordplay did I realize they were anagrams of TEMPORARILY as well. 

Seems all our hearts have gone out to Fiona after 84 across. Alas!

Still, they couldn't have operated and removed the hat? Couldn't be much more complicated than fixing pasture bloat as Gabriel does in Far from the Madding Crowd.

Whatever. Again, great puzzle!
My second fastest Sunday ever, at just under 21 minutes. I had no idea how the theme worked though, and needed to check the column to understand it - I appreciated it then.

I enjoyed this puzzle a lot! 

The one place I got stumped was the CYRIL/ILIA/MALAWI crossing (I had guessed Cyrus and had no clue about the other two)
RATATAT is familiar from Spelling Bee.
Clever theme but I got a PB without figuring it out.  Actually catching on to the theme might have slowed me down.
This one was lots of fun, thank you!

Wonderful puzzle, Curran! I really enjoyed this! After I solved 2 italicized clues, the revealer clicked for me, and I was able to solve all the other anagrams after that! Hope to see more puzzles from you!

that was a brain teaser if ever there was Curran - kudos! to celebrate here's my rendition of 'New York State of Mind' https://youtu.be/yGh9icvj1ss Billy Joel's classic love song to the city.. fritz free to boot
I got the trick as I filled in the very last square. I am not good at anagrams.
Aaargh! ERMA Bombeck comes up so often, you’d think I’d remember her name by now 😤

I enjoyed filling in the puzzle, but unfortunately did not get the trick without reading the column.  Then I grabbed scratch paper and worked the scrambles out.  Sure enough!  Congratulations to Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando who got married this weekend.  Hope he does bring her flowers sometimes.

Congrats to the setter/editor that knew that the Cyrillic alphabet was named after Cyril and not invented by him. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_and_Methodius Not sure I get what a MORALITY REP is. Do they represent MORALS? do they sell them? Do they report them? Do they repress them? A nice puzzle. Like many others I solved without getting the trick. Even the German contingent of the family prefers English scrabble.
My fastest Sunday ever. Under 17 minutes.  It was a little too easy for me. This was more like a Wednesday. I knew there was an anagram as the theme but didn't get it.
As often with themes, it was of no use in solving. Clever, but added nothing to the experience.

As a Bulgarian solver, I was disappointed to see CYRIL clued as “saint for whom the Russian alphabet was named after”. The Cyrillic script was developed in Bulgaria by disciples of Cyril and Methodius. Calling it the Russian alphabet feels inaccurate and frustrating especially after the communist era and Russification. The script is used by dozens of different languages, maybe it could have been clued as “Slavic script” or “Eastern European script”. Otherwise a great crossword, I just hope in the future the clue will be more accurate.

Can't fault the skillset in creating this puzzle and 'theme'. But as far as having fun solving it, it was mediocre. 

The biggest highlight was reading the editors notes and finding out the 'theme'.

All in all great craft, but not a particularly enjoyable solve.

On my first across pass, I skipped the italicized clues because they made no sense to me. I got PYRITE MOLAR with a few downs and thought "what the heck?" Then the revealer, at which point I went back to pyrite molar and thought about that one for a bit. Ohhhhhhh. Then it was fun to get the other theme answers using few crosses. Nice puzzle!
Pretty ambitious debut, Curran. It was fun trying to figure out the offbeat themers. "..when the wind don't blow in AMARILLO..." Townes Van Zandt: https://youtu.be/V0JWdsm5jJg?si=l8nJ8N3VW5ceFKJa

Fast solve but the theme never clicked for me. Learning of it from reading the notes registered as a “meh” from me. I suppose if anyone picks up on it early it would be helpful to solve faster. An ambitious theme to develop a puzzle around though.

The anagramming in the puzzle’s theme answers was quite impressive, although it didn’t register with me until I hit the revealer.  It would have been nice if the rest of the clues and entries had the same sparkle.
Another puzzle where we admire the craftsmanship, but don’t enjoy the solve.

Goodness, reading a fair few ‘too easy for a Sunday’ posts here, makes my struggle with it even more depressing!
Looking back I think it was the usual US suspects that threw me; ELMERS, I guess is a make of glue.  EVOO?? No idea. POP TOP. Ok.
On the upside, the African country and lake were gimmes. As for spitting camels, their Alpaca relations fire a mean mouthful if you get between them and their food. Which I frequently do while setting out said food. Talking about biting the hand that feeds you.

Very impressed with the constructor’s International pedigree, plus a Sunday debut. Kudos.
Breezy Sunday.  Congrats on your debut - having your first submission accepted is amazing!

Absolutely loved the theme on this one! So fun! I tried my own versions for fun:

1. Ruffled, just a bit?
PARTLY MOIRE

2. Tick bite while traveling?
AIRPORT LYME

3. Statement from a confident author, perhaps
"I RARELY OMIT"
It took me reading this article to finally get the theme. WOW! I love when a puzzle surprises me with a trick after I finish it, and this was one of my favorites.

I join the refrain of solving without understanding the theme before reading the column. Clever brain teasers that made some sense most of the time, though not always. Morality rep was my favorite.  Lego guy instead of man delayed my Mideast solve for a bit. Tough puzzle but as always,Thanks for my Me Time.

A very unsatisfying theme. Like many others, I had to read the blog to understand the theme. The problem seems to be the revealer. It is not a "literal description" of the theme answers. It is a cryptic description. Changing that one word could have made this a far better puzzle.

It appears I'm in the minority today - by chance I found myself mid-grid early in my solve, got 70A with barely any crosses, and immediately knew the answers to italicized clues would be anagrams of TEMPORARILY.

That said, it didn't really aid in my solve. It was easier/faster to answer the italicized clues with the easy crosses than to anagram anything.
Claude explained the theme to me. I was scratching my head. There was something annoying about this puzzle; clues just didn’t gel with me.
Wow! Very clever, a pleasure to wrestle with.

Brilliant puzzle.

Getting the revealer early on expedited the solve with five of the themed entries.  ROYAL PERMIT was Rosetta Stone.

Unfortunately, misreading the camel clue doubled the time spent on this.  Need to remember that Māori dance.

Holy debut, Batman!
And a little crunch to boot!

First submission? RLY?

Wowza.

And on the menu this week?
At least one

PORTLIER YAM.


(Ugh. Now we’re allll glad I wasn’t the constructor.)

Very cool theme! No idea until I read the column, so I kept wondering what the answers meant, especially since MORALITREP.

Thanks, and congratulations!

I never had to pause for more than a second or two while filling in this grid, and I ignored the theme until after the solve. But no complaints — I don’t mind a Sunday with Monday-level clueing and a cute, admire-after-solving theme.

Better than those Sundays where a handful of brutal entries are sprinkled throughout an otherwise easy grid (a recipe for a quick solve followed by a rough round of flyspecking).

🎶 Hey, Macarena… 🎶
Hello from AMARILLO!

[That special place for my cravats and bolos]
MY TIE PARLOR

 [“Come on, give it a shot, Vlad”]
O, TRY, IMPALER

You used the same eleven letters for all six theme answers?!?

THRIFT ZONE indeed!

Congrats on your debut!  Completed the puzzle without understanding the theme but good to know after reading the article.  

PS - PRIMETAYLOR for me is 1989, though I liked Reputation, Lover and Folklore too. 🤗

Since I stink at anagrams, I can appreciate this theme only vicariously.
All I could come up with was that the letters of the word TIME occurred out of order in each answer, which admittedly is not 1/10 as impressive as the actual theme.
Puzzle was fun but I wouldn't have gotten the theme in a thousand years.

I have a wispy concept of what to do with this puzzle, but this time I really lack the desire to pursue the Themers.  I am sorry to say it, but I filled the grid out of a sense of duty, but after a bad night (exacerbated by multiple visits from the cat:  "Mommy, mommy, let me under the quilt!...No, it's too hot! I'm leaving!") and an over-loaded list of Things to Do  (Which storage container has the sweaters?? And my warm socks?) I am quitting.  

I will enjoy reading others' experiences and emerge sadder but wiser, no doubt.
I didn’t get the theme until I read the column and my appreciation for the puzzle grew.

This was a tough one for me. I thought it might be an anagram, but kept on solving, hoping beyond hope that it was not. I hate anagrams (because I am really bad at them). I try, periodically to work out anagrams but my mind just doesn’t do it. 

This puzzle was nice because you didn’t have to get the anagram to solve, and the themed clues were fun to answer on their own. It was also very nice to not have a full grid of stock NYT crossword answers.
Basically just wrote the fairly easy answers in.  Didn’t pay any attention to the theme.  Yesterday was great. This was a long Tuesday.

For 44 across, I had SaT, rather than the correct SIT. This gave me, for 45 down, aCEHOTEL.

Now it happens that the last hotel I was in was The Clyde in Portland, Oregon, in April of this year. The Clyde has been called that since around the time the Titanic sank...except during a brief recent period when it was renamed The Ace, after which it went back to being The Clyde.

When it was The Ace, it was the second of a chain of hotels that had kind of a counterculture slant to it. The Portland Ace lent bicycles to its visitors to use to get around Portland. It had guitars in a lot of the rooms. It had a restaurant which was the starting point for the renaissance in mixed drinks that had swept the country. So the Portland Ace was, arguably, cool. Ditto the rest of the chain. (I missed most of this when I was there...the bicycles and the guitars were gone, although the record players remained).

So, aCEHOTEL, bizarrely, actually fit the clue, and blinded me to my mistake to the point that I had to look it up.

There was a woman at the desk of The Clyde whom I spoke to a few times. I was the long-haired, Asian-looking old man who walked into the lobby with a copy of Be Here Now by Baba Ram Dass in my hands, and told you the story about how I came to meet everyone, everywhere, all at once, but way too soon. If you read this, I wish you well.

I got PYRITE MOLAR and thought such a thing would be singularly unhygienic. (Fool's gold would rust in your mouth.) So there must be something else going on here. Figured it out with PRIME TAYLOR - letters are similar, no wait, they're the same! It's an anagram puzzle! Joy! No, I'm not gonna try to come up with one of my own without asking Claude for help.

Minifigs again, hi there YELLOW MAN. I had no idea that Lando Calrissian was the first one with natural skin tone. (See embedded article.) I actually have that one, but it was a special anniversary re-issue. One last note: there are actual gold C3PO minifigs that were handed out as prizes, like getting Wonka's golden ticket.

We have a feral cat problem in my neighborhood, and now I have to worry about feral hippos? That would be about the worst. Unless they were coked up or something. But how could that happen? https://www.cbsnews.com/news/baby-cocaine-hippo-rescued-colombia-pablo-escobar/

Very crafty! I solved the grid quickly but could not figure out the theme. I knew I needed to rearrange something, but I was focused on syllables and not letters! I had to come read the column to grok it. But I’m not disappointed! Hats off

As the peculiar themers came in, I had absolutely no idea what they were all about.  I tried Spoonerisms and different pronunciations. I looked for tricks in the clues rather than the answers. Then I gave up.  I got to TEMPORARILY OUT OF ORDER and pondered if MOLAR PYRITE would make more sense than PYRITE MOLAR.  It doesn't.

I wonder if, on a different day, with more sleep, I would have noticed the anagrams.  Anyway, today I didn't -- and when I couldn't make any sense of the theme answers and the rest of the puzzle felt pretty humdrum, I put down my pen and went to Rex to find out the trick.  I don't find it a very exciting one, btw, but I definitely should have noticed it

Whew. That was quite a workout, but one really amazing piece of construction. Just can't imagine what it took to come up with all those theme answers and then fit them all into the puzzle. And... ...a vaguely similar puzzle: A Sunday from June 1 of last year with the title "Making Arrangements". Must have done this one but had forgotten it. Anyway - some theme clues and answers: "LEGAL NICETY" GENETICALLYENGINEERED "EARTH" CHANGEOFHEART "GLIBNESS" MIXEDBLESSING "RESIST" TWISTEDSISTER "ROYAL PERMIT" TEMPORARILYOUTOFORDER And there were more. Here's that link: https://www.xwordinfo.com/Crossword?date=6/1/2025&h=117a ....

I don’t think I have ever been so bored completely such an OUTLANDISH puzzle. What a waste of a Sunday Crossword. 

🗑️ 🔥 

Rating:
2/10

Hippos in Colombia? Nice coincidence with everyone mourning Fiona.
Very nice debut - like many, I got the theme only after completing it (though the revealer should have cued me in). For some reason, last to fall was the Rachael Ray ingredient (EVOO) square - the cross of sewer/security system finally clicked.

For some reason, anagrams are very difficult for me. I don’t see them easily. I solved the puzzle grid, with the theme answers making little sense, but did not solve the theme. I thought I would feel dumb after reading the column with the theme explained. I didn’t because it wasn’t obvious. I just shrugged to myself, oh, well. Another theme that was oblivious to me. Pretty clever and, I would think, difficult to construct.
PB Sunday and my first under 30 min. Just flowed from top to bottom and never got stuck. Clueing was very straightforward. Fill not annoying. Theme by hindsight. Fine but not very challenging puzzle.
Not a particularly difficult solve despite not getting the theme until I read the column after. Truly one of the puzzles of all time!
This puzzle should be dedicated to Fiona the hippo. Great construct, even though I still don’t fully understand some of the answers!
Very clever! What an inspired debut! Not very challenging except for divining the theme, but just terrific in retrospect!
I had REPAIRMYTAR for longer than I’d like to admit—which ironically left me needing someone to REPAIRMYLOT

Just as I was about to ask for guidance on the "Common core" solution, it came to me. So, I'll waste space valuable blog space  by thanking Curran Eggertson and the EDS for reading my *Fiona* SATIRE yesterday. I understand it was a lot of trouble revising your entire puzzle at the last minute just for me, and I appreciate it... tons.

I RLY do not understand the theme, even after reading the column and a few of the commentators here. I'll delve in to it later this evening.

Bu the way... it's pronounced... _eyegore_
Lovely. Got the theme at exactly the halfway point and it helped with the trickier themed clues. Very impressive crossword, let alone debut. More please!

Insta-revealed the theme clues, so don’t have too much to say about that other than I’m glad I didn’t spend time on them.

The puzzle was okay. Knew about half of the entries from the first pass and then had to reveal a few names. I don’t think some of the answers work super well but I don’t care to elaborate further. 

Happy Sunday

Enjoyable. Had a typo at the bottom that hurt my time finding, but still under my Sunday average. Fair clues, no real groaner puns or nonsense.

I dug it.

Clever, I guess. But I solved this without any idea what the theme was, and so didn’t get to enjoy the “a ha” moment, as it were. But, well, sometimes it do be that way…. 

I also thought there were some poor clues that added to the tedium. I’m sure someone can enlighten me as to what EMS has to do with “Common core?”, but crossing it with OMG for “[Horrors!]” made for a little mess. Then we also have the house favorite SOYA appearing… a word no one says, least of all vegans (yes, I realize it’s being used properly and is  in the dictionary; no, that doesn’t make it a good clue/answer pair).  Those are just a few that stick out to me. 

Anyway, this is just one dog’s opinion…
Great puzzle!!! Congrats on your debut!🥳🎉

Fun puzzle, and I really enjoyed the theme! Knew as soon as I read the revealer clue that "out of order" would function as an anagram indicator, but it took a while to figure out exactly how.

The cluing on 19A is unfortunate, though - "he/she" is very often not an appropriate for singular "they".
Had to come here to get the anagram part of the puzzle after finishing the whole thing.

I liked seeing Wayne/MANOR in the puzzle as well as a Spanish red and yellow--RIOJA and AMARILLO.
And for BBT-watchers, who can forget Howard and the ROBOT ARM?
Had to get help on 125A because SODA technically works (R.A.D.s are skate shoes and this works for 116D). I guess it depends on how we'd define “many” in 125A.

Doable but lively puzzle. I actually used the theme to figure out some of the theme answers, which was nice. Especially MORALITYR__ and PRI_ETAYLOR.  Was very glad DJIBOUTI occurred to me with only a few crosses because I couldn't remember the spelling of the Spanish red. Curious how many complained about that one but not sure I'm curious enough to read all the comments to find out.

The only annoyance I had was not with the grid, but with the current focus management, which seems often to require an extra click to get back into the grid. Even worse in Spelling Bee.

Barry,
I tried to respond to you twice below but for some reason it's not going through.

I didn't think you were angry. I was responding to the previous respondent.

Fun puzzle. I enjoyed the cluing and the theme. 

Took a while to get the theme, but when I did, it was fun and helpful for checking my entries.

Re: 84A

Poor Fiona!  :(
Solved it then came here because I couldn’t figure out how the theme fit. Blew my mind, really impressive.

Fun, quick solve! However, I needed Wordplay to grok the theme because my plodding, leaden brain just couldn't come up with it. I tip my hat to those with the cleverness and mental agility required to figure it out, let alone create it in the first place.
13:09. fell into place very quickly today, didn’t even think about the theme until it was over
Anyone else groan after completing the MIDI?

They're anagrams.

Oh Boy.

A fun, very cosmopolitan feeling, puzzle that I solved basically as a themeless. Very neat theme though, now that I see it!  I wasn't trying to ignore it, I just kept filling things in and everything kind of felt fresh and fast that I didn't really think to stop and try to figure out what the revealer meant. I enjoyed the international flair.

I plugged in HIPPO right away because I had the h, but I had no idea there was a feral population of hippos in Colombia. The more you know.
I did not understand the Temporarily Out of Order until reading the explanation in Gameplay, but seeing it, I must hand it o you -- THAT was clever!
Took me embarrassingly long to understand the clue. Extremely impressive puzzle!
Well done!  It was fun to discover the theme, scratching your head wondering what on earth it might be, then it hits you like a brick.

Holy smokes! Tough one, worthy of a Saturday for me. I didn't understand the theme until I was in flyspecking mode when it dawned on me -- and shook me off MORALITY coP, which finally made everything fit into place.

For what it's worth, I've never heard of AVIA as a shoe brand, and had it as AVeA (ReAL for the Omani currency). The "I" was the last to fall, unlocking the music.

Lots of very clever cluing today, extra tricky, but I got my gold star. Phew!
Always excited for Sunday puzzles, and this one brought the joy! Well done on first submission and publication!

We are disappointed that Sunday puzzles are no longer available in alternate formats, in particular large print and left-handed. We like to work on the puzzled together, and the as-printed Sunday is too small for us to see.

I get it when there is a puzzle with graphics etc., but lately even straight Sunday crosswords aren't available in alternate formats

This is one of those puzzles that I solved without understanding the theme - without much difficulty in this case, possibly because I do the Down entries first. Reading the explanation here in Wordplay, I'm impressed that the constructor pulled it off!
I decided to do it without looking at Wordplay. Took a while to do it but succeeded. Good puzzle, fun for a rainy afternoon.
What a great debut!...congrats Curran and thanks for a quite crunchy Sunday puzzle. Esp enjoyed the Marine clue. Great play on words overall.

I did the whole puzzle in about my normal time, a little less, and at the end, I still didn't know how the answers relate to the big answer or the title of the puzzle.  This did not clarify it.  I got temporarily out of order almost immediately and that just threw me off to looking for anagrams rather than straight answers.
Fun puzzle. I absolutely could not see the trick with the theme answers, even after reading the solution.  I finally get it but it's rather annoying to not be able see it even with an explanation.
Enjoyable puzzle.  I hope you create more.

Great trick and properly executed.  A fine debut.  The constructor notes reveal that even more coherent and nonsensical answers were possible out of that little word.

Honestly I didn't enjoy the solving experience all that much, but that may have been my mood.  The African country/capital was completely alien to me.  And I spent a bunch of time flyspecking at the end before realizing they wanted spat and not spit.  Sigh.

Enjoyed it, thanks, Curran.

Macy's had long planned to brink back the Blue Hippo balloon for this year's parade. So now it will be in tribute to Fiona, and Macy's gave a large contribution to Fiona's zoo.
I didn’t get it even after finishing the puzzle but I came here to read about it and — I do enjoy it, really funny. Good job!

I’ve been a crossworder for 50 years and have enjoyed the
NYT Sunday puzzles. This puzzle was so fun when I realized the clues were anagrams of “temporarily”. I have not found many of the younger constructors to be very clever or interesting in their puzzle making, so this puzzle just made my year! I hope he continues to submit future fun puzzles for our enjoyment.

Very fun puzzle!  Genius theme that I didn’t see/understand fully until reading the column!  And I got the theme clue during the second go-round.  Loved most of the clues and breezed through fairly easily until I got to the southeast…found it pretty unfair to have two Spanish language clues crossing each other.  That was the last letter to fall for me and I pretty much had to run the alphabet to get it.  Other than that, bravo!  Lots of fun!

Wow, great puzzle! I was confused through a lot of it...got the revealer and kept thinking the words in the answer would be out of order in some way. I finished the whole puzzle and was still in the dark. Then I went to the Word Play column and read down to "charming, satisfying puzzle" and "fresh and interesting," and I thought okay, I need to give this one more try (to figure out the trick). And finally I got it!! So I'm glad I gave it that extra look; it was indeed charming and satisfying to see that they were all anagrams of TEMPORARILY! I am impressed! Fun Sunday; thanks Curran Eggertson.

There’s actually a practical reason for calling it a P-trap. It’s to differentiate it from older S-traps and U-traps. 

A U-trap is formed by a dip in a continuous horizontal length of pipe. You would find this only in older commercial buildings. An S-trap is formed when the pipe drops down vertically, curves upward, then drops back down and goes into the floor. This type of trap is banned in modern buildings because it lets sewer gas escape into the room. A P- trap has the pipe descend vertically, make a dip, then exit horizontally into the wall. Named because it resembles the letter P on its side. This is the modern standard.

How do I know all this, you ask? Am I a secret plumber? Nah, just a curious lady who googles.
